title: Sort rows by a value
summary: sort_values orders rows by a selected column. The other columns move with their row so names and scores stay matched.
introduction: sort_values orders rows by a selected column. The other columns move with their row so names and scores stay matched. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain sort rows by a value
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: sort_values orders rows by a selected column. The other columns move with their row so names and scores stay matched.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

ordered = df.sort_values("score")
print(ordered["name"].tolist())
blocks.title: Sort rows by a value

blocks.text: The output is ['Ben', 'Asha', 'Cara'], from lowest to highest score.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not sort each column separately; that breaks row relationships.
